summary: Decide the ten 1-1 splits, and re-examine id 164 on evidence that arrived after its demotion
logs: 10 splits to decide, plus a re-examination of id 164

decided.proposedName: msglm mk_msg_anthropic/mk_msgs_anthropic cache= / ttl= / cache_last_ckpt_only= — sets Anthropic's cache_control field; model-invisibility is Anthropic's documented assertion only (parent field id 164 was demoted the same day for lack of measurement), no independent evidence supplied
decided.reason: Source code (fetched live, github.com/AnswerDotAI/msglm/main/msglm/core.py) confirms the entry's mechanism claim is accurate: _add_cache_control/_remove_cache_ckpts only ever touch a sibling 'cache_control' key, never the 'text' value, and cache_last_ckpt_only just relocates which message carries that key. That part is true and not in dispute between the refuters. But PASS_METADATA requires establishing the field is one 'the model never reads' — and this project already litigated that exact question for cache_control itself (id 164, same day) and demoted it to CONTRACTUAL_ONLY, because the only argument for invisibility was 'it sits outside the content string,' which the role-field counterexample disproves as a general rule, leaving only Anthropic's documentation ('no effect on output token generation') as support — verified live today, verbatim, 2 hits on the control phrase, sentence present. id 11 is a thin wrapper that inherits that same field and supplies no new evidence: its own verifiedAgainst text admits it leans on 'an already-established-safe Anthropic field,' a status this project withdrew the same day. The refuter defending PASS_METADATA's strongest addition — a causal-attention/prefix-KV structural argument — is more sophisticated than 'position in JSON' but still ultimately requires trusting Anthropic's account of what their infrastructure does, which is documentation, not a measurement (no API key exists in this project to check). Repo sanity-checked independently (gh api: 15 stars, pushed 2026-04-06, not archived/disabled) — real, just not sufficient. Demoted to match its parent field's fate rather than narrowed, since the defect is in the evidentiary foundation itself, not in overclaimed scope.

decided.proposedName: Model-capability gate instead of hard-coded model-ID allowlist for enabling cache_control (scoped to field position outside tokenized content, not response-identity)
decided.reason:
Verified independently against the live page (docs.claude.com/platform.claude.com prompt-caching doc, both redirect to same 2,370,690-byte HTML, fetched raw 2026-08-18). Control phrase "cache_control" = 239 hits, proving a real, non-broken fetch.

Both refuters' cited quotes checked directly:
- Refuter 1's quote "Prompt caching has no effect on output token generation. The response you receive is identical to what you would get if prompt caching were not used." = 2 exact contiguous hits (rendered HTML + RSC JSON payload). Genuine, verbatim, accurately characterized.
- Refuter 2's claimed "1 hit, exact match" for "Prompt caching is supported on all active Claude models" = 0 hits for that contiguous string. The real payload has it split by an inline link: "Prompt caching is supported on all " + <link>"active Claude models"</link> + ".". The meaning is real (confirmed via the raw RSC fragment) but refuter 2's "exact match" claim is false as literally stated — sloppy, not fabricated, and not load-bearing for their core argument.

Deciding the entry required going past both refuters to the bar's actual wording. The bar's three prongs are narrow and concrete: different tokens read, different model answers, different amount of thinking. It does not ask "is the served response byte-identical." Refuter 1's quote answers a stronger, adjacent question (output-equivalence) that the entry doesn't need to win.

What the entry does need — "cache_control is a field the model never reads" — I verified directly from the docs' own code samples, not from the behavioral-equivalence sentence: `"cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}` appears as a sibling JSON key alongside `"model"`, `"max_tokens"`, `"system"`, `"messages"` in every example on the page (55 matches), never concatenated into a "text"/"content" string. That's a structural/schema fact about request layout, confirmed empirically from the live page's own examples — not an appeal to Anthropic's assurance about downstream serving behavior. It independently establishes: same tokens tokenized (cache_control isn't among them), same model targeted (model ID field untouched), same thinking config (no thinking/budget field touched). All three prongs answered "no" on structural grounds alone.

Refuter 1's P1/P6 argument would be right if the entry's ONLY support were the behavioral-equivalence doc sentence — that pattern is real and I'd apply it if that were the case. But there's a second, independent, structural basis here (field position in the documented schema) that doesn't require trusting Anthropic's output-fidelity promise, only the request schema — which is directly inspectable and was inspected. Capping at CONTRACTUAL_ONLY because a stronger, unnecessary claim also happens to be documented would be over-correcting past the bar as written, which the brief explicitly warns against.

Net: PASS_METADATA holds, but narrower than the entry's own one-line reasoning implies — "the answer is unaffected either way" overstates what's needed/proven; only "the field sits outside tokenized content" is required and that part is solid. Narrowing the name to reflect that scope per the register's convention.

decided.proposedName: Anthropic Prompt Caching (cache_control breakpoints, automatic mode)
decided.reason:
Independently re-fetched platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching as raw HTML today (200 OK, 2,370,690 bytes). Quote check first, per the rule: control phrase "Prompt caching" = 43 hits (fetch is good); the entry's exact quoted string "Prompt caching has no effect on output token generation. The response you receive is identical to what you would get if prompt caching were not used." = 2/2 verbatim hits, sitting in a bulleted "Exact matching" / "Output token generation" list. No fabrication, no inversion — the most-serious defect this register checks for is absent, confirming both refuters' quote-checks. Numeric claims also verified independently and unchanged: "10% of the base input token price" (1 hit), 1.25/2x write multiples and all four length minimums (512/1,024/2,048/4,096 tokens) present.

That settles quote integrity but not the tier fight, so I read the mechanism section myself rather than trusting either refuter's characterization. "How prompt caching works": the system checks whether a prompt prefix up to the cache breakpoint is already cached; if found it reuses it, otherwise it "processes the full prompt and caches the prefix." The "What invalidates the cache" table keys invalidation off actual content (tool defs, system block, messages) at each hierarchy level, not off cache_control's presence/absence. Together these establish, structurally and independent of the "identical response" assurance sentence, that cache_control is sibling JSON metadata attached to a content block — a breakpoint pointer for the server's prefix-cache lookup/store step — and is not itself tokenized into model input; the full content is unconditionally transmitted and is what's hashed/compared for a hit. This is architecturally the standard prefix/KV-cache pattern used industry-wide (vLLM, SGLang, etc.), not a claim we can only take on Anthropic's word.

That distinguishes this from the role counterexample the P6 pattern is built on: role is serialized into the chat template and becomes actual input tokens, which is exactly why position-in-JSON proves nothing for it. cache_control has no analogous job — nothing at generation time needs it — so the P6 shape-match the overturning refuter invokes doesn't actually transfer.

Applying the bar's literal test — different tokens read / different model / different amount of thinking — the answer is no on all three, and PASS_METADATA only requires "a field the model never reads changed," not bit-for-bit output identity across cache-hit/miss. The overturning refuter's demotion argument leans on residual doubt about decode-level floating-point nondeterminism from batching, which is a stricter standard than the bar asks for, and is a generic property of any batched inference server rather than something cache_control specifically introduces — importing it would sink PASS_METADATA/PASS_ABSOLUTE for nearly every live-API mechanism entry in the register, which isn't what "apply the bar as written" calls for. I could not independently check the cited id-164 precedent (not in front of me) so I gave it no weight. Uphold PASS_METADATA; name is accurate as-is ("automatic caching" is confirmed as a real, current named feature on the page), so no narrowing is warranted.

decided.proposedName: Token counting endpoint (/v1/messages/count_tokens): free and separately rate-limited per Anthropic's documented policy (not independently measured)
decided.reason: Own verification: fetched the live doc as raw HTML (2026-08-18, HTTP 200); control phrase count_tokens=35 hits / /v1/messages/count_tokens=10 hits confirms a good fetch. Quote 2 ("separate and independent rate limits...") is verbatim, 2 hits. Quote 1 ("free to use") is genuinely present but split across a <strong> tag, and the entry's version appends a comma not in the source while dropping the source's own qualifying clause ("but subject to requests per minute rate limits based on your usage tier") -- a selective splice, not a fabrication or inversion, but real. Applying the bar's explicit text: 'a documentation sentence...caps at CONTRACTUAL_ONLY. Only a measurement, or a structural argument that no request was ever sent, supports PASS_ABSOLUTE.' Both load-bearing claims here -- 'free' (a billing assertion) and 'separate rate limits' (a quota-bucketing assertion) -- are pure documentation sentences with no measurement behind them (no invoice audit, no rate-limit-exhaustion test) and no 'no request was ever sent' structural argument (a real HTTP request does go to count_tokens; what's asserted is how Anthropic treats it internally, which we can't verify from outside). That's the same P1 shape as 'provider says it declined to bill it.' The entry's one true structural point -- count_tokens can't alter the token sequence/model/thinking of a separate message-creation call, being an independent stateless endpoint -- is sound but isn't what the entry is built around; it claims no savings of its own and its whole content is the cost/rate-limit facts. Honest verdict is a narrower CONTRACTUAL_ONLY scoped to 'per Anthropic's stated policy,' not a flat PASS_ABSOLUTE.

decided.proposedName: prompt_cache_key routing-hint claim (OpenAI docs describe it as a routing/matching key; model-invisibility asserted by doc prose, never measured)
decided.reason: Independently re-fetched developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching today (200 OK, Last-Modified same day) and confirmed every quote/paraphrase in the entry is genuine: "approximately 15 requests per minute" (3 hits vs control "requests per minute" also 3 hits, so the fetch isn't broken), the "routed to a machine based on prompt_cache_key, with a hash of the initial prefix of the prompt as a secondary key" line, "A cache key improves routing but does not make different prompt prefixes match," and cached_tokens are all verbatim on the live page. No quote-fabrication problem exists here — both refuters were right on that point, so the split isn't about source integrity. I also pulled the actual JSON example myself and confirmed prompt_cache_key is a top-level sibling of "model", outside the "input" content array — the schema-position fact both refuters cite is real. But I searched the page for any sentence stating the field is invisible to the model / excluded from the forward pass ("not visible", "not sent to the model", "does not influence", etc.) and got zero hits — the page only ever describes a routing/matching mechanism, never asserts model-invisibility. That means the entry's central claim ("never rendered as prompt content to the model") rests entirely on the entry author's inference from a documentation description of server-side routing, not on anything the doc states outright and not on any measurement — no one ran the test that would actually settle it (identical prompt, varied prompt_cache_key, compare output/logprobs). The client-visible JSON position proves what we send, not what OpenAI's server forwards into the model after processing; that gap is closed only by trusting OpenAI's account of its own internal pipeline. The bar is explicit that a documentation sentence is the provider's word and caps at CONTRACTUAL_ONLY, and the entry's own provenance field admits "primary-doc" as its sole basis. The upholding refuter's rescue attempt (re-grounding in "the parallel-key/hash-comparison mechanism") still draws only on the same doc prose, so it doesn't change the evidence tier — and this isn't the "different mechanism decides what gets produced" over-correction the brief warns against, since that was about inventing an extraneous disqualifier, not about applying the bar's own explicit documentation-sentence cap. A narrower PASS_METADATA scope doesn't rescue it either: the unresolved fact (does this field ever reach the forward pass) is unchanged by how tightly the name is scoped, so this is a genuine demotion to CONTRACTUAL_ONLY, not a narrower pass.

decided.proposedName: Gemini explicit context caching (cache-hit requests omit the cached bytes from the wire; token-identity is provider-asserted)
decided.reason:
Independently re-fetched all three live sources (raw HTML, cookie-jar double-fetch — first hit is always a 302 to the devsite oauth shim, second hit with the cookie jar returns 200; this matches what the uphold refuter reported and I confirmed it myself rather than taking their word for it):
- ai.google.dev/api/generate-content (200, 1.21MB)
- ai.google.dev/api/caching (200, 333KB)
- ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing (200, 248KB)

Quote check (Hard Rule 4), with a control phrase: the uphold refuter's cited verbatim string "The name of the content cached to use as context to serve the prediction" returns 0 raw `grep -o` hits on either page — but that is a tag-interruption artifact, not a fabrication: Google's devsite wraps text in per-token `<span>` tags for syntax highlighting. After stripping tags with a script (not markdown conversion, matching Hard Rule 3's intent — I preserved raw content, just removed markup) the phrase appears verbatim, exactly once, as the description of the `cachedContent` field on `GenerateContentRequest`, on **/api/generate-content** (not /api/caching, which is where the refuter's citation was ambiguous but not wrong — they cited both pages together). Control phrase "cachedContentTokenCount" hit 2/2 as expected, so this isn't a broken-fetch zero. The quote is genuine. This is NOT a case of the "five entries caught quoting text not on the page" pattern.

Pricing/telemetry facts I re-verified directly (all match the uphold refuter's numbers): Gemini 2.5 Flash $0.30→$0.03 caching (90%); Gemini 3.7 Flash $0.75→$0.075 (90%, promo storage $0.50/1M-tok/hr through 2026-12-31 then $1.00 from 2027); Gemini 2.0 Flash $0.10→$0.025 (75%) — and the live page does carry "Warning: Gemini 2.0 Flash is deprecated and has been shut down June 1, 2026," confirming the staleness catch (dead comparator, correct arithmetic — non-core, doesn't move the verdict on its own). Also confirmed `model` on `CachedContent` is "Required. Immutable." — structurally forecloses a "different model answers" failure mode.

None of that is where this entry actually breaks. The break is the classification of the core neutrality claim, and here I side with the overturn: the entry's own reasoning states "no prompt bytes are omitted from the model's effective context, only from the wire" — which is a concession, not a rebuttal, of the P1 test. I confirmed the mechanism directly from the schema: `cachedContents.create` takes the real content once; every subsequent `generateContent` cache-hit call carries only `cachedContent: "cachedContents/{id}"`, a resource-name string. The actual content is not on the wire for that request — full stop, verified from the field list, not inferred. The claim that the model nonetheless reads an identical effective token sequence on that call is exactly the API reference's prose ("...to use as context to serve the prediction") — i.e. THE PROVIDER'S WORD, which the bar caps at CONTRACTUAL_ONLY regardless of how well-documented or industry-standard the pattern is. `cachedContentTokenCount` doesn't rescue this to a measurement: it's a number Google's own server reports about Google's own cache, not something the customer measures independently. A functional check ("ask about the cached content, get the right answer") shows the model has access to consistent information; it doesn't establish token-for-token identity with an inlined call, which is what THE BAR actually asks.

This also isn't PASS_METADATA: that tier requires "only a field the model never reads changed." Here the omitted material is not a field the model ignores — it is precisely the content the model is meant to read, just resolved server-side from storage rather than carried on this request. That's a different shape than Anthropic's `cache_control` (content is resent in full every call; only an ignorable annotation is added — directly observable, no trust required) sitting in the same batch. It isn't PASS_ABSOLUTE either: a request is sent on every call; "structural argument that no request was ever sent" doesn't apply to a cache-hit `generateContent` call that still goes out over the network.

This is a genuine, real, well-documented mechanism — not a fabrication, not a FAIL. But its behavioral-equivalence claim rests entirely on Google's documentation of how `cachedContent` resolves server-side, which the customer cannot observe or measure from their own request/response. That's CONTRACTUAL_ONLY as written in the bar, and the narrower title reflects exactly what is and isn't provider-asserted rather than discarding the entry's verified pricing/telemetry work.

decided.proposedName: AWS Marketplace private offer drawing down existing EDP/PPA commitment (trap's "fully deployed on AWS infrastructure" eligibility-restriction claim struck — verified fabricated/inverted: the May 2025 AWS change expanded Marketplace SaaS eligibility to non-AWS/hybrid/on-prem deployments, it did not restrict it)
decided.reason:
Did my own verification rather than just weighing the two refuters, on both halves of the entry.

MECHANISM (core PASS_ABSOLUTE claim): sound. An AWS Marketplace/EDP private offer is a billing-routing/settlement arrangement — which committed-spend ledger an already-incurred charge is paid against. It is negotiated at the contract layer, once, and has no effect on the InvokeModel/Converse/Messages request itself: same bytes on the wire, same model invoked, same amount of thinking. This is a structural "no request changed" argument, not reliance on a documentation sentence about what the provider does internally, so it isn't capped at CONTRACTUAL_ONLY. Both refuters agree on this and I independently concur — nothing here is telemetry-detectable or wire-visible, which is exactly what makes it PASS_ABSOLUTE-shaped.

QUOTE CHECK (the deciding issue): I fetched the raw HTML of the exact AWS "What's New" post refuter 2 cited (https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/05/aws-marketplace-saas-products-deployment-locations/, dated 2025-05-05, title/date matching the trap's "May 1, 2025"). Control phrase "AWS Marketplace" = 22 hits (fetch is good, page loaded). Entry's quoted phrase "fully deployed on AWS infrastructure" = 0 hits. The page's actual body (pulled from postBody JSON, not paraphrased): "AWS Marketplace now supports software as a service (SaaS) products deployed on AWS, on other cloud infrastructures, and on-premises." The headline itself is "AWS Marketplace now supports SaaS products from all deployment locations" — the literal opposite of the entry's claimed restriction. The only nearby phrase is "100% deployed on AWS infrastructure" (2 hits), which is criteria for an optional "Deployed on AWS" badge, not an eligibility gate. I also checked AWS's own private-offers buyer guide (docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/buyerguide/buyer-private-offers.html — the doc that actually governs the mechanism this entry is about): control "private offer" = 36 hits, quoted phrase = 0 hits, zero mentions of any deployment-location eligibility restriction at all. So this isn't a reachability gap (refuter 1's "source-unreachable" position doesn't hold up — the page is trivially fetchable) — it's a confirmed, inverted fabrication: AWS expanded eligibility in May 2025, the entry says AWS restricted it.

Per the standing rule, a fabricated/inverted quote is the most serious defect available and decides the entry regardless of whether the mechanism is sound — so the entry cannot stand as published with its trap/estimatedReach claims intact. But the false material sits in an auxiliary caveat field (trap/estimatedReach), not in the sentence the PASS_ABSOLUTE verdict actually rests on (the billing-routing/zero-wire-effect claim), so the honest remedy is the narrower one: keep PASS_ABSOLUTE for the verified mechanism, strike the fabricated eligibility claim via the name rather than failing a structurally-sound entry over a bad caveat. Side with refuter 2's finding on the quote (independently reproduced) over refuter 1's unverified "upheld," and land where refuter 2 itself landed: correct/strike, don't kill.

Fabricated citation, self-verified with control phrase: the entry quotes "the strict bar's own definition of PASS_METADATA" as saying 'Anthropic cache_control... [is] the canonical example.' Grepped SCHEMA.md (the actual contract, tests/registerSchema.test.ts enforces it): "canonical example" = 0 hits; control phrase "only a field the model never reads changed" (the real definition text) = 1 hit, so the search is sound and the zero is real. The closest real text, in the working register (2026-08-10-strict-identity-register.md:71), says "The largest lever by a wide margin" -- not "canonical example." All 11 repo-wide hits for that phrase sit inside candidate/verdict JSON files under adjudication, never in a rules document -- entries citing each other in a circle and calling it the rubric. Per my explicit brief, a fabricated quote decides the entry regardless of mechanism soundness.

Independent of the fabrication, the mechanism claim -- "cache_control is a field the model does not read as prompt content" -- is the identical unproven "outside the content string, therefore invisible" argument that this same register's own audit, dated the same day (docs/research/2026-08-18-passing-column-audit.md), already ran against cache_control's home entry (id 164) and demoted PASS_METADATA -> CONTRACTUAL_ONLY: role is a same-schema counterexample sitting outside the content string that the model demonstrably reads, so position in the JSON proves nothing, and absent a wire measurement this is Anthropic's documented assertion, which SCHEMA.md caps at CONTRACTUAL_ONLY. Entry 136 just extends the same unmeasured claim across Anthropic/OpenAI/Vertex. It was never checked against this precedent -- it's absent from the audit's own named list of 15 siblings resting on that argument -- which is the gap refuter A (overturned/CONTRACTUAL_ONLY) caught and refuter B (upheld) didn't weigh as dispositive.

CONTRACTUAL_ONLY rather than FAIL because the register's own established remedy for both this exact mechanism (id 164) and this exact defect (id 74, the other fabricated-quote sibling in the same audit) was CONTRACTUAL_ONLY, not FAIL -- the pricing/telemetry facts refuter B re-verified live are accepted as accurate, they just don't answer the tier question. No scope-narrowing rescue applies (unlike ids 102/125): the flaw is uniform across all three named providers, so the name is unchanged and only the verdict tier moves.

decided.proposedName: Duplicate/fan-out billed requests from Bifrost's OpenAI→Anthropic streaming-fallback bug (single unconfirmed report, maintainer's evidence request unanswered 5+ weeks)
decided.reason:
Independently verified live via `gh api` (not cached), 2026-08-18.

CONFIRMED FACTS: maximhq/bifrost is real, 7,405 stars, pushed today — not a fabrication concern. Issue #5128 exists, title/body match the entry's description; the reporter's body does say "doubling API costs" verbatim (control phrase grep: 1 hit, so the fetch itself is sound and the underlying quote-like language is genuine). Issue state: OPEN, filed 2026-07-13 by a single reporter (ace331), 3 comments total: a CodeRabbit auto-plan bot, a human reply from akshaydeo (verified via `gh api users/akshaydeo` — real co-founder/CTO of maximhq) asking "can you share the screenshot of the dashboard and an example?", and a third comment containing an off-domain "agent-cost-auditor" tracking link with a paid remediation offer — spam/promotional, not from the reporter, given no weight. The reporter never answered the maintainer's request. "Relevant logs/output" in the issue is empty. 5+ weeks later, still unconfirmed and unreproduced by anyone.

Grepping the live issue+comments for the entry's own telemetrySignal claims ("session/trace ID," "matching prompt-token counts") returns 0 hits for "trace," "token count," and "session" — that specific detection mechanism is not grounded in the cited source; it was invented and presented as if derived from it.

Cross-referenced the two linked PRs (#5221 closed/unmerged, #5170 open/unmerged): both fix a narrower, different bug (#5169, malformed SSE for reasoning-delta streams crashing the anthropic-python SDK). One contributor's PR description *speculates* this "independently explains" #5128 "for reasoning-capable models" — an unconfirmed hypothesis buried in someone else's unmerged PR, never linked by a maintainer as fixing #5128.

Neither refuter alleged a fabricated or inverted quote from the entry itself (both marked quoteCheck "no-quote-to-check"), so the quote-fabrication tiebreaker does not decide this one — the entry doesn't put source text in quotation marks that turns out wrong. What decides it is the bar's own evidentiary requirement: "Only a measurement, or a structural argument that no request was ever sent, supports PASS_ABSOLUTE." Neither exists here. There is no measurement (the maintainer's explicit request for a dashboard screenshot went unanswered), and the "structural argument" rests entirely on one anonymous, unconfirmed, disputed bug report — evidentiarily weaker than "the provider's word," which the bar itself caps at CONTRACTUAL_ONLY. The entry's own fields overstate this posture by calling it a "confirmed GitHub issue" and describing "A/B isolation" as already "described" when the thread contains only a one-line unsubstantiated claim, no attached logs, and an open maintainer challenge.

I agree with refuter 1 that the underlying mechanism, if real, has the right shape for PASS_ABSOLUTE (the canceled streaming request's output is discarded and never delivered, so eliminating it changes nothing about what's sent to the user — pure waste removal, not a delivery-path change). But mechanism-soundness is not sufficient under this bar; the fact itself has to be established, and here it is a single, disputed, non-reproduced practitioner report that the vendor's own CTO has been unable to get evidence for over five weeks. That is squarely INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, not a pass at any tier — narrowing the name (Bifrost-specific, single-source) does not cure a claim that isn't established at all, only a claim that's established-but-overreaching in scope. This is not the "different mechanism decides what gets produced" over-correction flagged as out-of-bounds elsewhere; it is a direct application of the bar's own measurement-or-structural-proof requirement.

Independently fetched the live Anthropic prompt-caching page myself (2,370,690 bytes, matching refuter 2's byte count) and grepped it directly, with control phrases ("prompt caching"=67, "cache_control"=239) confirming a good, non-broken fetch. Quote 1 in the entry ("Cache breakpoints themselves don't add any cost") is verbatim, 1 hit, correctly contextualized under "Understanding cache breakpoint costs." Quote 2 in the entry -- "cache different sections that change at different frequencies (tools rarely change, but context updates daily)" -- returns ZERO hits as a continuous string. I traced why: the source has two DIFFERENT sentences in two DIFFERENT sections -- (a) under "Explicit cache breakpoints": "...you need to cache different sections that change at different frequencies, or need fine-grained control over exactly what gets cached," and (b) under a separate later heading "When to use multiple breakpoints" (a bullet under "You can define up to 4 cache breakpoints if you want to:"): "Cache different sections that change at different frequencies (for example, tools rarely change, but context updates daily)." The entry welds clause (a)'s opening to clause (b)'s parenthetical, silently drops "for example,", and presents the splice in quotation marks as one continuous verbatim quote -- text that appears nowhere on the page as written. This is a genuine fabricated composite quote (confirmed zero-hits by my own grep, not merely alleged), not the minor substance-preserving edit refuter 1 characterized it as. Per the standing instruction that a fabricated or inverted quote decides the entry regardless of whether the underlying mechanism is sound, the otherwise-solid Aider source-code mechanism proof (add_cache_control only appends metadata to an already-assembled message dict) does not rescue the entry. This is a fabrication case, not a scoping case, so a narrower pass is not the honest remedy -- refuter 2's FAIL verdict is correct and I reach it independently.

Demotion upheld, not overturned — but on a firmer, self-checked basis than the recorded one. I re-fetched https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching myself today as raw HTML (curl, HTTP 200, 2,370,690 bytes — matches the audit brief's own byte count, confirming same page/version) and grepped it directly rather than trusting any prior refuter's report. Control phrases confirm the fetch is good and current: "cache_control" 239 hits, "ephemeral" 187 hits. Against that valid fetch, every distinctive fragment of entry 164's core evidentiary quote — presented under a "Directly confirmed this session" claim — returns ZERO hits: "serving/pricing directive" 0, "purely a serving" 0, "not read by the model as content" 0, "stripped out before processing" 0, "receives only the text value" 0. The bare word "stripped" does appear (4x) but exclusively in an unrelated passage about thinking-blocks being stripped from context on older models — nothing to do with cache_control. This is a fabricated quote dressed as a verified one, the identical failure mode this register already used to sink entry 74 (near-identical invented phrasing: "serving-side directive," "stripped out before processing," also 0 hits) and that two sibling refuters independently caught on entries 60 and 166 in the same cluster. I did not rely on their reports for id 164 itself — I reproduced the zero-hit result fresh, against a fresh fetch, myself.

The recorded correction note demotes 164 solely on the role-counterexample/P6 argument ("position in JSON proves nothing"), and the new sibling evidence has a real point against that specific argument in isolation: role is a counterexample because it is demonstrably chat-templated into tokens (documented, and behaviorally testable by any customer — swap user/assistant, watch output change), whereas cache_control's documented job is prefix-hash KV-cache matching, a different functional category. Several sibling entries (42, 68, 173) built a sharper, non-role-dependent structural argument around that distinction and survived review on it — so as a critique of the STATED rationale, the sibling pushback is fair. But it doesn't rescue 164, for two independent reasons. First, 164 has its own dispositive problem the role debate never touches: its central quote is fabricated, which alone caps it per this register's own precedent (74) regardless of how the P6 argument resolves. Second, even granting the sibling entries' sharper mechanism argument its full due and applying it charitably to 164, that argument — "the full prefix is always transmitted intact; cache_control only marks a boundary; a cache that silently altered keyed content would break its own hit/miss accounting" — still terminates in Anthropic's own description of how their prefix-hash cache-matching pipeline is ordered relative to tokenization. That ordering (does the server strip the field before or after the tokenizer sees it) is not observable from outside Anthropic's serving stack. A customer can observe their own request construction (trivially: they never wrote cache_control into their own text field) and response-side telemetry (cache_creation_input_tokens / cache_read_input_tokens, hit vs. miss) — and a TTL-swap-same-content experiment against that telemetry is a real, describable test that would show whether TTL enters the cache KEY — but nobody has run it in this project (confirmed by the 2026-08-18 audit brief itself: "Nothing was measured... needs an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY this project does not have," and by every refuter in the sibling sweep who touched this field). And even a clean result there would only characterize the hash key, not the tokenizer input.
